```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

A study in surveyframe passes through 5 stages: design the questionnaire and
its analysis plan, collect the answers, check them, run the planned analyses,
and write the report. This page runs each stage in R. The `.sframe` file it
writes opens in SurveyStudio too, so a study can move between the 2.

The examples use the `paired` demo, a training evaluation measured before and
after. Its data is demonstration data, not collected from participants, and
every output made from it says so.

For a guided tour at the R console, run `demo("tour", package =
"surveyframe")`. The `verify` guided tour seals an instrument, changes a copy
and shows the integrity check with `demo("verify", package = "surveyframe")`.

## Open a study

```{r}
library(surveyframe)
d <- sframe_demo("paired")
d
```

To open a study of your own, read its file:

```{r}
ins <- read_sframe("my_study.sframe")
```

## 1. Design

The parts are built with `sframe_item()`, `sframe_choice_set()`,
`sframe_scale()` and `sframe_instrument()`. The plan is a list of blocks in
`sframe_instrument(analysis_plan = )`. `write_sframe()` saves the file with
its integrity hash.

```{r}
write_sframe(d$instrument, "paired.sframe")
```

Before collecting, write the plan down. `render_report()` given the instrument
alone writes the pre-analysis plan, a document to submit to OSF, Zenodo or an ethics
committee.

```{r}
render_report(d$instrument, output_file = "paired-plan.pdf", format = "pdf")
```

## 2. Collect

```{r}
export_survey(d$instrument, "paired-survey.html",
              endpoint_url = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/.../exec")
export_google_sheet(d$instrument, sheet_url = "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/...")
```

## 3. Check

```{r}
responses <- read_responses("paired-responses.csv", d$instrument,
                            respondent_id = "respondent_id")
sframe_quality_results(responses, d$instrument)
```

## 4. Analyse

`run_analysis_plan()` runs the declared plan, as declared.

```{r}
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
results
```

## 5. Report

```{r}
render_report(d$instrument, d$responses, output_file = "paired-report.docx",
              format = "docx")
```

The report names the instrument's hash, so a reader can check that the
questionnaire analysed is the one planned.

## Prefer to point and click?

The same 5 stages run in SurveyStudio. See
[Run a study in SurveyStudio](run-a-study-in-surveystudio.html).
